div.p: Augmented Reality (AR) is rapidly evolving and reshaping how people engage with digital content, offering experiences that feel both immersive and interactive. This paper presents an AR-powered mobile application designed to enhance the way users visualize furniture and plan interior spaces. The system is built as an Android application, developed in Kotlin using Android Studio, while the backend is handled through PHP and MySQL with phpMyAdmin support. Through the app, users can browse a catalog of 3D furniture models and virtually place them within their real environment using their device's camera. They can scale, rotate, and position objects in real time, helping reduce uncertainty in design decisions by providing accurate spatial visualization. Compared with existing AR interior design solutions, our application demonstrates lower latency, a cleaner and more intuitive interface, and more efficient backend processing. The system's effectiveness was measured through functional testing, user feedback, and response-time analysis, showing strong user satisfaction and reliable performance. Overall, this work contributes to the growing use of AR in interior design and highlights how combining mobile platforms with AR technologies can transform the decision-making process for both clients and designers.

Integrating AR into interior design directly addresses many long-standing challenges faced by designers and clients. Typically, spatial layouts, color schemes, and material selections must be visualized through drawings or renders, leaving clients to imagine the final result. This often leads to miscommunication and costly changes later in a project. With AR, however, furniture, lighting, and de´cor can be virtually placed, modified, and visualized in real time within actual spaces [1], [3], [6]. This hands-on approach provides clarity, reduces uncertainty, and enables clients to make informed decisions with confidence.

The technology also transforms the designer-client relationship. Instead of being passive recipients of expert advice, clients actively participate in the creative process-experimenting with layouts, finishes, and accessories from the comfort of their own homes. Designers, in turn, benefit from clearer communication, faster feedback, and fewer misunderstandings, making the design process more collaborative and efficient. Advanced AR features, such as real-time measurement tools, lighting simulations, and even AI-driven design suggestions, further enrich the experience [5], [15], [25].

Beyond professional practice, AR is also shaping education and retail. Interior design students can now experiment with virtual furniture and lighting setups in immersive learning environments, enhancing creativity and practical readiness [18], [20]. On the consumer side, retailers are increasingly offering AR-based "try before you buy" solutions, allowing customers to visualize products in their homes. This not only boosts customer confidence but also reduces return rates, directly benefiting businesses [21], [23].

Recent advancements in mobile platforms such as Google's ARCore and Apple's ARKit have made AR applications easier to build and deploy than ever before [17], [24]. When combined with AI, IoT, and cloud technologies, AR has the potential to deliver highly adaptive and personalized design solutions. For example, applications can suggest layouts based on user lifestyles, enable remote collaboration across locations, and even simulate sustainability outcomes such as energy efficiency [16], [19], [25].

In short, AR is not just a small improvement in the design workflow-it represents a fundamental shift in how spaces are imagined, communicated, and realized. By merging human creativity with computational power, AR offers design experiences that are smarter, more sustainable, and deeply engaging [6], [8]. As the technology continues to mature, the boundary between imagination and reality in interior design grows thinner, allowing both professionals and clients to bring their dream spaces to life with unprecedented accuracy and ease. adaptability, and automation continue to define the next frontier for AR-driven design innovation.

div.head: II. LITERATURE REVIEW
div.p: Recent studies on Augmented Reality (AR) in interior design have explored various approaches, each showcasing the growing potential of AR in enhancing design visualization and user interaction (Table I).

For instance, Markerless Augmented Reality Application for Interior Designing [17] presents a real-time markerless AR system that helps users visualize room layouts and furniture placement with improved realism. While effective for visualization, it shows limited adaptability under different lighting and room conditions. Similarly, Interactive Interior Design Using Augmented Reality and 3D Modeling [16] combines AR with 3D modeling to create immersive interior environments, though the system remains at a prototype stage without large-scale validation.

ARchitect: Visualize Your Dream Space with Augmented Reality [15] focuses on user customization, allowing homeowners to modify and preview interior layouts through a mobile interface. However, its functionality centers mainly on visualization rather than automated design assistance. In the same direction, RoomifyAR: Rendering Multiple Models to Design a Room [24] enables users to view and position several 3D objects simultaneously in AR, enhancing spatial comprehension. Yet, the application experiences reduced performance when handling larger 3D assets.

Finally, Smart Interior Design System Leveraging ML and Augmented Reality for Personalization [25] introduces a datadriven approach that combines machine learning with AR to provide tailored design suggestions. Although innovative, the framework is still in its early phase and needs further testing for practical usability.

Collectively, these studies emphasize AR's growing role in transforming interior design through realtime visualization, user customization, and intelligent personalization. OVERVIEW OF AUGMENTED REALITY Augmented Reality (AR) is an interactive technology that enriches human perception by overlaying virtual elements-such as 3D models, images, animations, sounds, or text-directly onto the real world (see Figure 1). Unlike Virtual Reality (VR), which immerses users entirely in a digital environment, AR enhances the real-world view by adding contextual digital layers to it [7], [8], [11]. These overlays are typically delivered through smartphones, tablets, AR glasses, or headsets equipped with cameras, sensors, and software capable of tracking orientation and recognizing physical objects in real time.

The process behind AR involves capturing a live view of the environment, interpreting it using computer vision algorithms, and then projecting virtual objects with accurate positioning and scaling. This creates the illusion that digital elements coexist naturally within the physical surroundings, adapting dynamically to user movement, lighting, and perspective [9], [10], [11]. AR applications now span a wide range of industries. In retail, it enables customers to preview furniture, accessories, or clothing before purchase [23]. In education, AR simplifies complex concepts through interactive 3D content that enhances understanding [5]. In healthcare, it helps surgeons overlay medical imaging, such as MRI or CT scans, onto patients' bodies to perform precise procedures [11]. Industrial applications use AR to assist technicians in inspecting and repairing machinery through real-time guidance [14].

div.p: For interior design and architecture, AR has proven especially valuable. Designers and clients can visualize furniture, color schemes, and spatial layouts in real environments, improving decision-making and reducing planning errors [1], [3], [6], [16]. Popular consumer-level AR applications-such as IKEA Place and Poke´mon GO-have demonstrated how AR can scale to mainstream use, turning visualization into an engaging and interactive experience [19], [8].

To meet user expectations, AR systems must deliver smooth, real-time rendering and accurate tracking. Development kits like Google ARCore and Apple ARKit have significantly improved precision, spatial detection, and lighting estimation [17], [24]. Future trends point toward lighter wearable devices, AI-driven personalization, and seamless integration with IoT for adaptive environments [25].

Ultimately, AR represents more than just a visual enhancement-it signifies fundamental change in how people interact with their surroundings. By merging computational intelligence with physical space, AR narrows the gap between digital imagination and tangible experience, transforming industries and daily life alike [6], [8].

div.head: IV. AR IN INTERIOR DESIGN
div.p: Within interior design, Augmented Reality (AR) serves as a powerful bridge between conceptual ideas and real-world experiences for both designers and clients. By projecting 3D models of furniture, lighting, de´cor, and architectural elements into actual spaces, AR enables real-time customization without the need to physically move objects. Using smartphones, tablets, or AR glasses, users can scan a room and virtually place items with accuracy in scale, proportion, and orientation, making the design process more engaging and error-free [1], [3], [6], [16].

One of the most significant benefits of AR in this field is the ability to visualize space and design elements in real time. Clients can immediately see how furniture, flooring, or artwork would look in a given environment, reducing uncertainty and helping them make confident decisions before implementation [15], [17]. The interactive aspect of AR also empowers users to adjust features such as color, size, texture, and material on the spot. This flexibility transforms interior planning into a collaborative and creative process where multiple design options can be explored instantly [5], [15], [16].

Traditionally, interior design presentations relied on 2D drawings or static renderings, which often led to misunderstandings and costly revisions. AR overcomes this challenge by allowing immersive walkthroughs-either on-site or remotely-so that clients can preview proposed spaces as if they already existed. This streamlines communication, speeds up approval cycles, and ensures better alignment between designer intent and client expectations [4], [19], [20].

Additionally, AR platforms often include precise measurement tools, such as virtual rulers and spatial mapping, that guarantee furniture and fixtures fit accurately within a room. These tools minimize errors, optimize layouts, and enhance the functionality of living spaces [13], [14]. Beyond professional practice, AR is also becoming a key tool in education. Design students can experiment with layouts, lighting, and materials in simulated environments, gaining practical insights without being constrained by budgets or physical resources [5], [18], [20].

On the consumer side, retail adoption of AR has grown rapidly. Major furniture and home de´cor brands now offer mobile AR applications that let customers "try before they buy." By virtually placing items in their homes, users gain confidence in purchase decisions, which in turn reduces return rates and strengthens customer satisfaction [21], [23].

Overall, AR transforms interior design into an interactive, collaborative, and highly personalized experience. Instead of relying solely on imagination, clients can actively participate in shaping their spaces. As AR technologies continue to evolve-integrating artificial intelligence (AI), IoT devices, and cloud-based collaboration-the future points toward design solutions that are adaptive, data-driven, and deeply usercentered, where the digital and physical blend seamlessly to create functional and emotionally resonant spaces [6], [8], [25].

div.head: V. PROPOSED ARCHITECTURE
div.p: Interior design is undergoing a rapid transformation thanks to Augmented Reality (AR), which allows users to preview how furniture, lighting, and de´cor will appear in their own spaces before making decisions. AR provides an immersive and interactive platform that turns design into a hands-on experience. The proposed system in this paper is a mobile AR-based application that combines a Kotlin-based Android front end with a PHP-powered backend and an SQL database managed through phpMyAdmin. This architecture is designed to ensure high performance, accurate AR rendering, efficient data processing, and secure storage management. The system follows a modular three-layer client-server architecture:

Frontend (Mobile Application): The Android application, developed natively in Kotlin, serves as the primary interface for users. Built on ARCore, it detects room surfaces, dimensions, and lighting conditions through the device camera. Users can then place, resize, and rotate 3D furniture models in real time. By running natively, the application ensures low latency, smooth rendering, and seamless interaction with device sensors. It also supports secure logins, user profile management, and design history synchronization.

Backend (Server Layer): The backend, implemented in PHP with Visual Studio, processes all requests from the mobile application through RESTful APIs. It handles core logic such as verifying furniture-room compatibility, filtering options based on style and size, and retrieving relevant 3D models. Beyond basic operations like authentication and session management, the backend is designed to be scalable, enabling future extensions such as collaborative design, AI-based recommendations, and cloud rendering for more complex AR interactions.

Database (Data Layer): The SQL database, managed via phpMyAdmin, stores persistent data including user accounts, room dimensions, furniture metadata, and design histories. Its relational schema allows efficient querying and ensures data consistency across modules. For example, users can search for furniture that fits specific style or dimension constraints. The system also records user interactions, which can later be used for personalization or machine learning-based predictive design. ACID compliance ensures reliability, even under heavy workloads.

Interaction Flow: The design workflow begins when the user logs into the app and scans their room using the AR interface. The captured spatial data, along with selected furniture preferences, is securely transmitted to the backend. The server processes the data-validating dimensions, retrieving 3D models, and applying rules-and sends a structured JSON response back to the mobile app. The AR environment then renders the updated scene in real time, giving users immediate visual feedback. Continuous data exchange between client, server, and database guarantees a smooth, interactive experience where users can iteratively refine their designs.

This architecture not only provides stability and scalability but also positions the system for future enhancements such as cross-platform integration, AI-driven personalization, and cloud-based collaboration features. Figure 2 illustrates the overall workflow and interaction between the mobile application, backend server, and database. VI. METHODOLOGY A review of prior works shows that most AR-based interior design applications are developed using cross-platform frameworks like Flutter or game engines such as Unity3D. While these approaches provide wider device compatibility, they often introduce performance overhead and limit optimization for specific platforms. In contrast, our system takes a native development approach, using Kotlin in Android Studio with direct integration of ARCore. This decision ensures tighter hardware-software integration, reduced latency, and optimized memory handling-all of which are critical for delivering a seamless AR experience [6], [16], [23], [24].

div.head: A. Backend Development:
div.p: Many existing AR design systems rely on managed cloud platforms such as Firebase for real-time synchronization and data storage. While convenient, these services impose limitations on customization, scalability, and hosting control. To address this, our system employs a custom backend developed in PHP using Visual Studio Code, structured around RESTful APIs [4], [10]. This provides greater flexibility in managing business logic, user sessions, and third-party integrations, while keeping future scalability in mind.

div.head: B. Database Management:
div.p: For data storage, some solutions in the industry favor NoSQL systems like Firebase Realtime Database. These options are suitable for rapid prototyping but lack efficiency for handling relational queries, data integrity, and structured relationships. Instead, our system implements a relational MySQL database managed through phpMyAdmin. This enables normalized schema design to organize users, room measurements, 3D model metadata, and design histories efficiently. It also supports complex queries-such as filtering furniture models based on both style and size constraints-while ensuring ACID compliance for reliability under high loads [4], [25].

div.head: C. Development Process:
div.p: Unlike many commercial AR applications that use agile or iterative methodologies for rapid deployment, this work follows a structured, phase-wise development lifecycle, aligning with academic project requirements. Each phase-from design to implementation and testing-was carefully planned, with user feedback incorporated at every stage [15], [18], [20]. This approach ensures modifications are based on real usage data rather than assumptions, improving both system robustness and user satisfaction.

div.head: D. ARCore Utilization:
div.p: The proposed system relies exclusively on Google ARCore to deliver AR functionality. ARCore offers advanced features such as motion tracking, plane detection, and light estimation, which enhance object placement accuracy and realism [9], [10], [11], [24]. By focusing on a single platform instead of combining ARCore (Android) and ARKit (iOS), the system avoids cross-platform overhead, leading to more stable performance across all tested Android devices.

div.head: E. Evaluation Strategy:
div.p: To assess system performance and usability, a multi-level evaluation strategy was adopted:
Usability Testing: Conducted using the System Usability Scale (SUS) to evaluate ease of use and overall satisfaction [21].
Performance Benchmarking: Metrics such as frames per second (FPS) and API response times were measured to ensure responsiveness [6], [16].
User Acceptance Testing: End-users tested the system in real environments, validating the app's accuracy and overall effectiveness [1], [3], [5].
By combining quantitative benchmarks with qualitative user feedback, the evaluation provided a comprehensive understanding of the system's performance in real-world use cases [20], [25].

div.head: A. Result:
div.p: The implementation of the proposed AR-based interior design application yielded notable improvements across visualization, interaction, and communication. As illustrated in Figure 3, users could seamlessly view life-sized virtual furniture, decorative elements, and architectural features integrated into their physical environment. This realistic visualization allowed them to better understand proportions, spatial relationships, and overall design coherence-an advantage traditional 2D drawings or static 3D renders cannot offer [1], [3], [6], [16]. User interaction was smooth and responsive. Furniture models Fig. 3. Output illustration of AR applications in interior design could be moved, rotated, resized, and recolored in real time, enabling a trial-and-error design process that felt both intuitive and engaging [5], [15]. The built-in measurement tools demonstrated high accuracy in capturing room dimensions and ensuring that virtual objects fit appropriately within the space. This significantly reduced errors in layout planning and optimized furniture placement [13], [14].

From a communication perspective, the system enabled immersive walkthroughs that allowed designers and clients to explore proposed layouts together, either on-site or remotely. This interactive review process minimized misunderstandings, accelerated approvals, and cut down on costly design revisions [4], [9], [20].

Beyond professional design contexts, the application was tested in educational settings where interior design students reported increased motivation, creativity, and spatial awareness when compared to conventional teaching methods [5], [18]. In retail scenarios, customers using the app to preview furniture in their homes exhibited stronger purchase confidence and fewer product returns, demonstrating the technology's practical value in commercial use [21], [22], [25].

div.head: B. Discussion:
div.p: The results confirm that AR offers transformative advantages for interior design. Unlike static blueprints or prerendered visuals, AR merges virtual and physical elements in real time, creating an immersive and experiential understanding of design decisions. Clients become active participants in the process, experimenting with different layouts, finishes, and color schemes rather than passively observing proposals. This collaborative environment fosters clearer communication, faster feedback, and stronger alignment between designer intent and client expectations [6], [9], [23].

The system's precision measurement tools further highlight AR's ability to optimize spatial planning-a critical requirement in modern interiors where functionality is just as important as aesthetics. Educational applications of AR also point toward its long-term role in training future designers by offering immersive, risk-free environments for experimentation [18], [20].

However, challenges remain. Initial costs for AR technology, device compatibility issues, and user adaptation barriers are considerations that must be addressed for broader adoption [7], [11]. Nonetheless, the rapid evolution of AR platforms such as ARCore and ARKit, combined with AI-powered design recommendations and IoT integration, promises to overcome many of these hurdles in the near future [23], [24]. Future research may focus on extending AR beyond visualization to include sustainability analysis, smart home integration, and collaborative cloud-based design tools [19], [25].

In summary, the findings demonstrate that AR significantly enhances visualization, personalization, and decision-making in interior design. By bridging the gap between digital imagination and physical reality, AR establishes itself as a practical, user-friendly, and forward-looking solution for professionals, students, and consumers alike [6], [8], [25].

div.head: VIII. FUTURE SCOPE
div.p: While the proposed AR interior design application demonstrates strong potential, several opportunities exist to expand its functionality and impact in future iterations.One promising direction is cross-platform deployment. Currently optimized for Android using ARCore, the system can be extended to support iOS devices with ARKit integration, as well as webbased solutions through WebXR. This would allow broader accessibility without requiring users to download a dedicated application.Another area of development lies in artificial intelligence (AI) integration. By leveraging machine learning algorithms, the application could deliver personalized recommendations suggesting furniture styles, colors, or layouts based on user preferences and behavior patterns. In addition, implementing advanced rendering techniques such as ray tracing would enable more photorealistic visualizations, making virtual objects nearly indistinguishable from real ones.From a technical perspective, cloud storage and synchronization could be adopted to support multi-device continuity. For example, users could begin designing a space on a smartphone and seamlessly continue on a tablet or desktop. Cloud services such as AWS, Firebase, or Google Cloud could also support persistent AR scenes, enabling users to save and revisit design projects tied to physical spaces-an especially useful feature for long-term renovations.Integration with e-commerce platforms such as Amazon, IKEA, or Wayfair presents another opportunity. By linking AR visualizations directly to online catalogs, users could purchase furniture and de´cor items directly within the application, streamlining the path from design to purchase. Similarly, collaborative design modes could allow multiple users-such as family members, friends, or professional designers to view, modify, and comment on designs in real time, regardless of their location.Advanced interaction methods also represent an exciting direction for growth. Features such as voice commands, gesture recognition, and computer vision-based tracking could create more intuitive ways to manipulate objects in AR. Furthermore, integrating VR modes would allow full walkthroughs of virtual interiors, offering clients an even deeper sense of scale and spatial flow before committing to design decisions.

Finally, the application can extend beyond residential interiors into commercial domains, supporting office planning, retail layouts, and event space visualization. By combining AR with IoT-enabled devices, future systems could even simulate environmental conditions such as lighting, temperature, or energy consumption-paving the way for smarter, more sustainable interior design solutions.In essence, the future scope of AR in interior design points toward a highly adaptive ecosystem where digital and physical spaces converge. With AI, cloud collaboration, and IoT integration, AR applications will evolve from visualization tools into comprehensive platforms that support creativity, efficiency, and sustainability.

div.head: IX. CONCLUSION
div.p: The proposed Augmented Reality (AR) interior design application demonstrates how AR can fundamentally transform the way users visualize and plan living spaces. By combining ARCore-based spatial mapping with a native Android front end built in Kotlin, and a PHP-MySQL backend for data management, the system delivers a smooth, scalable, and user-centered design experience. Users can preview furniture, de´cor, and layout arrangements in real-time within their actual environments, turning abstract concepts into tangible visualizations. Testing and evaluation confirmed strong performance across usability, responsiveness, and visualization accuracy. Users reported high levels of satisfaction, particularly with the intuitive interface, the precision of virtual object placement, and the ability to make design decisions with greater confidence. For retailers, the system also provides a valuable channel to engage customers more effectively, reduce product return rates, and drive purchase decisions.This work highlights how AR is no longer limited to experimental or entertainment applications but is becoming a practical and commercially viable tool for design and consumer decision-making. The approach taken in this study focusing on native Android development and a structured backend ensures both efficiency and reliability, while also laying the groundwork for future expansion.Looking ahead, the system can be further enhanced with features such as AI-driven design recommendations, cross-platform support, collaborative modes, and advanced spatial analysis for precise measurements. By continuing to integrate AR with emerging technologies like IoT, cloud computing, and photorealistic rendering, future versions of such applications will not only improve visualization but also create intelligent, sustainable, and deeply personalized design solutions.In conclusion, the project provides a strong foundation for bringing AR into practical consumer-grade interior design. It bridges imagination with reality, empowering both clients and designers to make informed, creative, and confident design choices.
